objectClass.primaryType: freestanding domed medieval masonry bake oven with attached preparation table
objectClass.notes: The dark arched cavity, thick dome profile and open iron door must read as a real oven volume; a flat facade or black painted arch is a hard failure.

reasoning: The object combines a continuous dome with discrete stone courses, brick arches, roof tiles, chimney and timber worktable.
A believable mouth requires tunnel depth, interior floor, embers, loaves, door thickness, hinge alignment and soot response.
Preparation, cooling and firewood zones must remain visible without turning the footprint into scattered clutter.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex depth is required by masonry repetition, true arched cavity, hinged door, tiled roof, chimney and food/tool material systems.

unknownsToResolveBeforeImplementation: The hidden rear dome and flue path are inferred from standard masonry construction.
Embers use emissive geometry and a restrained local light rather than volumetric fire.

details.description: A broad asymmetrical plastered dome swells behind the brick facade with chipped edges and soot-darkened crown contact.
Irregular fieldstone blocks form the raised plinth, lower firewood arch, side walls and projected ledge.
Wedge-like terracotta voussoirs form a full arched mouth with separate jambs, threshold and mortar seams.
The mouth opens into a deep soot-blackened tunnel with a tiled floor and visible rear darkness.
A thick arched iron door swings open from aligned side hinges and has a central strap, rivet row and latch handle.
Restrained orange coals and charred logs illuminate two browned loaves inside without filling the cavity with flame.
Rows of curved chipped terracotta tiles overlap across the short rain hood and chimney cap.
A square lime-mortar chimney has four open vent gaps, soot-darkened inner walls and a small tiled cap.
Black soot blooms around the mouth, under the hood and down the chimney while leaving irregular plaster islands.
The attached table uses a thick flour-worn top, four legs, lower shelf, stretchers and visible iron pegs.
A wicker proofing basket, scored raw dough, open flour sack and earthenware jug use distinct silhouettes and surfaces.
A long wooden peel, rolling pin and handle lie fully supported across the preparation surface without floating.
Three irregular browned loaves rest on a separate iron-bar cooling rack under the table.
Split logs with pale end grain stack inside the lower stone arch and retain visible air gaps.
A long iron rake and poker lean against the right ledge with dimensional tines, shaft and wooden grip contact.

anatomy.note: Object domain; character anatomy is not applicable.

definitionOfDone: The deep arched oven cavity, dome, brick and stone construction, hinged door, restrained embers, tile/chimney system and complete baker workstation remain readable from main and side views.

qualityCriteria: Fieldstone plinth, plaster dome, brick arch and chimney form a believable thick oven volume.
Deep cavity, threshold, soot, hinged door, restrained embers and interior loaves remain distinct.
Curved tile rows and vented chimney cap retain overlap, thickness and open gaps.
Braced table, dough, flour, baskets, peel, cooling loaves, firewood and tools remain supported and visible.
Stone, brick, mortar, plaster, soot, iron, oak, bread, linen, wicker and embers respond independently.

antiShallowSpecRules: A flat masonry facade with a dark painted arch may not pass.
The door may not float or hinge from its center.
Roof tiles may not be one corrugated slab.
Embers may not overexpose the cavity or hide the bread.

authoringInstruction: Assessment completed from the admitted reference before implementation.
